anuttara_01: In this highest state of supreme God consciousness there is no need of spiritual progress, no contemplation, no art of expression, no investigation, no meditation, no concentration, no recitation, exertion or practice. Tell me then, what is the supreme and well-ascertained truth? Listen indeed to this! Neither abandon nor accept anything, enjoy everything. Remain as you are!
anuttara_02: In reality, there is no such thing as birth and death, so how can the question arise of bondage for living beings? There never was any such bondage for the one who is entirely free, and therefore, to struggle for liberation is useless and nothing more than delusion — like a dark shadow mistaken for a demon, or a rope seen as a snake. Neither abandon nor accept anything, remain as you are, well established in your own Self.
anuttara_03: In the oneness of that supreme state of anuttara, what talk can there be, and what differentiated path of adorer, adored and adoration? Wonder of wonders! Though it appears differentiated, this illusion is no other than consciousness, one without a second. Everything is nothing but the pure essence of your own Self-experience, so why worry in vain?
anuttara_04: One cannot compare the bliss of this state to the intoxication of wealth or wine, nor to the union with a beloved woman. This excessive joy of the Self is comparable only to the weight of that blissful state which descends when one gets liberated from all differentiation. The flow of this supreme consciousness is nothing other than your own treasure abode that you had temporarily forgotten.
anuttara_05: Attraction and repulsion, pleasure and pain, rising and setting, self-confidence and depression; all these states with which the universe is formed shine as mutually different but in reality, they are not. Whenever you perceive the specificity of some thing, at that very moment perceive the essence of your own consciousness as one with it — why not take delight in the fullness of that awareness?
anuttara_06: In this world the totality of objects appear eternally in the present moment. Differentiated action is an illusion based on the unlawful pervasion of an intermediate state which is unreal, transient, fraudulent, just a heap of appearances like the illusion of a dream. Remain above these defects forged by doubt — be awakened!
anuttara_07: For the insentient there is no outflow of objective things, for those are manifested only when experienced by thee. Though deprived of reality they share reality in one instant through erroneous perception. Thus the greatness of this universe arises from your own imagination — it does not take birth from anything else. Therefore you alone shine in all these worlds, and though one, you become many by your own glory!
anuttara_08: Real or unreal, small or plentiful, eternal or momentary — this universe rising from your own consciousness and becoming one with your essence appears glorified in the mirror of Consciousness. Having ascertained the sublimity of the universe, enjoy universal sovereignty.
bhairava_01: Great God, pervading all moving and unmoving things, pure spirit, one, eternal, infinite, refuge of the helpless — with my mind filled with Thee, I worship Thee in my loving heart.
bhairava_02: By the energy of your grace it has been revealed to me that this vibrating universe is your own existence. O Lord Shiva, you are my own soul, and as such this universe is my own expression and existence.
bhairava_03: O possessor of everything, though your devotees are caught in the net of destiny that arouses troubles and bondage, still they are not afraid of the fret and fever of this world. Fear exists only when there is someone else to inflict it — but when there is none other than You, how can fear arise?
bhairava_04: O angel of death, do not look towards me with wrathful and frightening eyes, for I am always absorbed in the worship of Lord Shiva. One with the energy of the terrifying Bhairava, your dreadful looks can do me no harm.
bhairava_05: O Lord Bhairava, I offer salutations to you who has awakened me to the realization that everything in existence is you alone. The darkness of my mind destroyed, I fear neither the demons of karma nor Yama, the Lord of death.
bhairava_06: O Lord Shiva, through real knowledge I realize all attachments and all that exists is activated by you. My mind saturated with immortal devotion, I experience supreme bliss.
bhairava_07: O Lord, sometimes misery torments my mind, but at that same moment, blessed by a shower of your grace, a clear vision of my oneness with you arises, and my mind feels appeased.
bhairava_08: O Lord Shiva, charity, ritual bath and penance subside worldly troubles — but even more, remembrance of your sacred words pours a stream of peace into my heart.
bhairava_09: O Lord Bhairava, through my utmost faith I have perceived you in the unique sacrifice of oneness. Filled with your presence, my consciousness dances and sings, enjoying its own ecstasy.
bhairava_10_phala: I, Abhinavagupta, composed this hymn on the tenth of the dark fortnight of Pausha. By its meditation and recitation, merciful Lord Bhairava swiftly destroys the torments of this wilderness of worldly existence.
bpc_01: He is one, within and without, the unfailing form of all lights and darknesses; both radiance and darkness are His.
bpc_02: He alone is the Supreme Lord, the very nature of all beings; all that arises is His power, steeped in lordship.
bpc_03: Power does not seek separation from the Possessor of power; their oneness is eternal, like fire and fuel.
bpc_04: He alone is Bhairava, God, whose nature is sustaining the world; all reflected by His power resembles His own Self.
bpc_05: His supreme Goddess yearns to touch His own form; in all existences His fullness is neither less nor more.
bpc_06: This God, united with this Goddess, ever eager for divine play, simultaneously creates and destroys the manifold universe, being all-powerful.
bpc_07: That He accomplishes what seems most difficult is His unsurpassed freedom: this is sovereignty, lordship, and the very form of consciousness.
bpc_08: Limited brightness is the mark of the inert; consciousness differs from inertia because it cannot be measured or bounded.
bpc_09: Thus, for the independent One who enjoys His own power, creation and dissolution abide as His very nature.
bpc_10: In them is endless variety: upward, downward, across; worlds, their parts, and the extremes of pleasure and pain.
bpc_11: Full knowledge of this is called freedom; for the deluded, that very thing is the fearsome samsara.
bpc_12: It comes from the essence of His grace, from guru, Agama, or any scripture of the Supreme Lord, from whatever source.
bpc_13: Knowledge of that reality is liberation from the Supreme Lord; for the awakened, its fullness is known as living freedom.
bpc_14: Bondage and liberation are not divided from the form of the Supreme Lord; in truth, no distinction exists in Him.
bpc_15: Thus Bhairava, resting on the lotus-trident of will, creativity, knowledge, and power, is contemplated as the nature of all beings.
dhs_01: The body is called God's temple; the Self is the eternal deity. Cast off ignorance's garland and worship Him with the feeling 'I am He.'
dhs_02: I salute Ganapati, praised by hosts of demons and gods, ever intent on granting desired boons, the best of all sights, worthy of worship, whose body is life.
dhs_03: I salute the youthful Bhairava named Apana, whose feet are worshipped by hosts of heroic yoginis and streams of siddhas, who removes the suffering of the humble.
dhs_04: By whose power the world shines to devotees as Shiva's path, I always salute that stainless true Guru, whose form is attention.
dhs_05: I salute that consciousness-filled Bliss-Bhairava, whom the goddesses of the senses ever worship in the heart-lotus with their enjoyments of sense objects.
dhs_06: I salute that Bliss-Bhairavi, whose form is reflective awareness, who ceaselessly plays at the world's arising, manifestation, and devouring.
dhs_07: I constantly bow to that Brahmani, whose form is intellect, who, stationed on the petal of the Lord of Gods, worships Bhairava with flowers of resolve.
dhs_08: I salute that Shambhavi Mother, whose form is ego, who, stationed on fire's petal, ever worships Bhairava with flowers of pride.
dhs_09: I salute that Kaumari, whose form is mind, who, moving on the southern petal, ever worships Bhairava with flowers of distinction.
dhs_10: I constantly bow to that Vaishnavi Power, whose form is revelation, who, moving on the southwest petal, worships Bhairava with flowers of sound.
dhs_11: I bow to Varahi, stationed in the western mandala, skin-clad, pleasing Bhairava with heart-stealing flowers of touch.
dhs_12: I praise Indrani, embodiment of sight, seated in the wind-direction mandala, of surpassing form, who worships Bhairava.
dhs_13: I bow to Chamunda, called Tongue, dwelling in the Lord of Wealth's lotus, ever worshipping Bhairava with diverse six-flavored foods.
dhs_14: I ever bow to Mahalakshmi, called Smell, seated in Isha's lotus, who worships Bhairava with manifold fragrances.
dhs_15: I praise the ever-giver of accomplishments, called Self, Lord of the Field, worshipped in six systems, enfolded by thirty-six tattvas.
dhs_16: I bow to the wheel of presiding deities of one's own body, ever arising thus, essence of pulsing experience, constantly present within all.
stc_001: Through sweet, mind-stealing speech, through Paśyantī, through manifestation, the Supreme Lord's blissful majesty triumphs.
stc_002: Expanded by the wealth of gracious compassion-awareness and supreme bliss, His greatness lit by knowledge, the Unconquered One triumphs.
stc_003: Salutations to the infinite Light, ocean of Śaṅkara's milk, whose Self is pure nectar, spreading as point and sound.
stc_004: We hate You, we praise You; we chant to You, O Lord of Ambika. Very attainable, You have well sustained our world.
stc_005: Salutations to Śambhu, the Lord who is withdrawn-contact union, born of perfect nectar, and all-pervading Māyā in nature.
stc_006: We salute Pārameśvara, the universal form undivided in divisions and uncut in all that can be severed.
stc_007: Salutations to the Immovable, smaller than Om's half-mātrā yet vast, whose quality is attributelessness beyond the cosmic egg.
stc_008: We praise the Swan-Power of the Lord-Swan who pervades space and moves everywhere, carrying the cosmic egg in her womb.
stc_009: Without any material support He alone paints the world-picture on the wall; salutations to the Trident-bearer, glory of the arts.
stc_010: O Hara-Hamsa, grant us here Śiva's self-milked knowledge, purified after being drawn from Māyā's web-womb.
stc_011: We offer ourselves to You, the Existing One, the one reality of ultimate truth, undivided amid distinctions delimited by the six means of valid knowledge.
stc_012: May we behold Your deep, lovely cave, free of darkness, encircled by supreme light, and enter within.
stc_013: Salutations even to those who, even in dream, behold the Lord with moon-digit-adorned crest, giver of supreme bliss.
stc_014: O Lord, the taste for cultivating the state of being, skilled in cutting rebirth's fear, pleases all; whom does it not delight?
stc_015: O Lord of the world, as long as life lasts, may this be our duty: by Your grace, to abide with one-pointed mind on You.
stc_016: Homage to Śambhu, whose being is the Vedas and Āgamas spreading in a thousand branches, the wish-fulfilling tree yielding endless fruits.
stc_017: O Lord, applying speech, mind, and bodily acts to You, may we become imbued with You, free from duality, somewhere, somehow.
stc_018: Homage to the Trident-bearer, endowed with independent power in the reality-grounded ordering of worlds' creation and dissolution.
stc_019: Let even the name of the great Matted One beyond qualities, chief object of meditation, be contemplated—what fruit from other supports?
stc_020: Praiseworthy are those who rely on the power of the mantra 'Namo Namaḥ Śivāya' and strive to enjoy Śāmbhava splendour.
stc_021: O Lord, what path fails to reach You, what speech fails to speak You, what meditation fails to contemplate You—what exists that You are not?
stc_022: May this essence—'He is worshipped, meditated upon, and pleased'—flow in a thousand streams and increase in me toward You.
stc_023: Homage to You, Lord, Immovable Pillar, wearing a serpent as sacred thread, whose Self is the abode of the garland of all leaves of wisdom.
stc_024: O Bhava, Your remembrance is the one medicine for ignorance's darkness; by granting this and that, may Your grace work in me.
stc_025: Salutations to Īśa, fulfiller of every human aim; even the obeisance of the wise here is fitly offered to Him.
stc_026: Drowned in the fearful ocean of saṃsāra, the home of sorrows, those who attain Śarva, the jewel of devotees' hopes, conquer all.
stc_027: O Dhūrjaṭa, You are known to those whose treasure is unobscured, non-dual, steadfast knowledge; who indeed are these that know You?
stc_028: Though without qualities, He is the sole object of the knowledge of guṇas; the Unborn triumphs. Though desireless by nature, He is the highest fruit of desires.
stc_029: O Vibho, the milky ocean of majesty, not won by gods' striving for fortune's jewel-nectar, is naturally Yours alone.
stc_030: With devotion I bow for humanity's liberation; O Bhava, protect them; to Śambhu, auspicious and fearless, giver of remembrance and dance.
stc_031: All-knowing, all-doing, You are all—so say the wise. What is knowable or doable, Lord, that is not offered by You to the Infinite?
stc_032: Your will alone bears the fruit of the three worlds—O Lord, who knows how far Your works extend?
stc_033: Even Brahmā and others ascend again and again on the stairway of His deeds to reach His abode; I bow to Him.
stc_034: This Brahmā, this Mahendra, these two, sun and moon—thus the vine of His power blossoms; may that Bhava protect us.
stc_035: Even deluded minds cannot bring him error; his end is hard for far-goers, yet he is gentle to the praiser.
stc_036: Salutations in praise, remembrance, meditation, sight, touch, and attainment to the mass of bliss, compassionate, matted-haired.
stc_037: O Lord, even when my mind asks, 'What is this delight?', by delight I am yours; not in myself—what joy!
stc_038: Though I ponder countless duties and my mind is fickle, resting beyond being and nonbeing, may I delight greatly in bliss.
stc_039: O Lord, if your subtle form is only a fraction of the three worlds, how could your gross form fail to charm even Brahma and the rest?
stc_040: O God, if you alone were not what these words express, what anguish would the wise endure in the net of speech!
stc_041: O Lord, by what sequence, act, or insight may the teaching 'You are visible' bring grace to me?
stc_042: Salutations to the matted-haired one, without motive, sole benefactor of the three worlds, desired by all yet free from desire.
stc_043: Ah, this knowledge of the field serves the great aim of the good: by it they plant in you, O Lord, devotion of endless fruit.
stc_044: O Enchanter, how vast is your illusion! Even after gaining the treasure of meditating on you, the deluded world grows lax.
stc_045: At the outset, be everywhere, whether as act or instrument; let the world exist, yet You alone are its free doer.
stc_046: Who but You has the power or compassion to lift the three worlds, seized by the duality of the three qualities and three vibrations?
stc_047: O God, what fault is a fault resolved to attain You? What merit is merit resolved not to attain You?
stc_048: O God, great is this act of meditating on You; in it, who from Brahma down is not qualified for our liberation?
stc_049: The start of every undertaking, the finish of every act, and the varied thoughts between: O Lord, these lie on the path of Your mind.
stc_050: O Lord, no higher expansion of joys, thousandfold richer, is seen anywhere except in the nectar of devotion to You.
stc_051: Homage to Lord Soma, moon-adorned, who gathers desire and stretches its range.
stc_052: Powerless and without resolve everywhere, what can I do? The all-gracious Shakti, Shankari, is my refuge.
stc_053: O Lord, beyond qualities, whose Self is defined as complete transcendence, in what part is Your supreme reflection found?
stc_054: O Lord, though You are the non-dual, conditionless Self, even now Your measurable maya deceives us.
stc_055: O Bhava, attainment of powers, eternal sovereignty, and end of becoming are the tender leaves on the wish-fulfilling tree of devotion to You.
stc_056: Here, every direction is soaked in worldly time. Even having gained this, when will you reach its end, O Lord? Tell me.
stc_057: I bow to Śambhu, the Great Swan, sole dweller in the peaceful, virtuous mind, radiant with abundant glory.
stc_058: May the lamp of awakening to You be mine, O Lord, the lamp of devotion burning the heart's proud darkness and all the fuel of saṃsāra.
stc_059: Who but You, O Hara, is the poet able to project and reabsorb the three-world drama, teeming with countless seeds of existence?
stc_060: I bow to the Free and the Bound, who can turn being into non-being or non-being into being, sole master of dissolution and lordship.
stc_061: Whatever joy appears even within the three worlds is only a drop of Him; I salute that God, the ocean of bliss.
stc_062: Ah, blessed are Brahmā and the rest who, liberated, chant the glorious tale 'Obeisance to Śiva,' overcome with joy.
stc_063: Salutations to You, O Bhava: though desireless, You create endless desires; though beginningless, You enjoy the universe.
stc_064: We seek no benefit in praising the Lord, primal root of the three worlds' beginning, since He is perfect dharma.
stc_065: Even great, excellent purpose-fulfillers are stained by delusion’s mass; remembering Him, minds grow clear; praise auspicious Śiva.
stc_066: O Lord, Your sovereign power here is inviolate; by Your will alone the three worlds dissolve and arise.
stc_067: Even evil offered to You becomes supreme merit, O Lord; since You are nowhere else, even merit finds its worth in You.
stc_068: Seizing Him in the fist, they cry, ‘We have seen You; where will You flee?’ Though devotion is beyond attainment, the blessed hasten to Śiva.
stc_069: We praise You, beyond the purest essence of Rig, Yajur, and Saman; O profound, beautiful One, You are the Vedas’ knowable Self.
stc_070: O Paramēśvara, You are the Ordainer, beginning and end of the universe; if not from You, whence could the host of dharma arise?
stc_071: Salutations to You, O God: You raise and shatter the world’s bewildering delusion; veiling non-dual knowledge-bliss, You reveal it.
stc_072: To whom could finite distinctions be offered by any wish? May Śiva, catching Māyā in one blink, guard us from it.
stc_073: O Lord of lords, You uphold the sublime path of dispassion, the supreme radiance of knowledge, and the utmost summit of desirelessness.
stc_074: You are Brahman even to Brahmā; O Ruler, whose lord are You not? Who knows how far You are the blessing of the world’s blessings?
stc_075: What need of other kin, friends, or masters? Everywhere, O my Lord, You are the rescuer from the ocean of existence.
stc_076: Victorious are those who can wash away stains of delusion and māyā, drawn by Śaiva yoga's power and sprinkled with divine nectar.
stc_077: May the Lord whose brilliance the Gāyatrī sings, inspiring all minds, inspire our minds onto the good path.
stc_078: O Eight-formed Lord, will You not give us eternal stability in even one form? If pleased, You will do all.
stc_079: The truth of things generally produces meaningful action; from You, O Lord, even Your name grants fulfillment unto liberation.
stc_080: By Your power that repeatedly conceives each varied state of this wondrous world, Lord, what wise person is not amazed?
stc_081: We remember Cupid's foe, whose one heroic remembrance makes difficult things easy and sorrow joyful.
stc_082: Victorious are songs whose theme is the Supreme Lord, by whose name even great souls bristle with joyful rapture.
stc_083: If supreme being is just as You are, You are the withdrawal of the threefold world's beginning, spread by Your own power's array.
stc_084: You are mantra, worthy of mantra, and its master; apart from You there is none. Grant me that mantra, Lord, that I may become Your mantra.
stc_085: O Lord, You are Being itself, true resolve, the Self I too am; what is this saṃsāra, this dream in You?
stc_086: That indestructible, inaccessible, one, well-founded: O Lord, it is sovereignty for those who offer action’s fruits to You.
stc_087: Able to crush every calamity, to grant or withhold every blessing, that Bull-bannered God of gods is our merciful Lord.
stc_088: The divine eye of knowledge, blinded by māyā’s impurity: Lord, devotion to You is the supreme ointment that cleanses it.
stc_089: Grant me the fearless, blissful, one, imperishable state; come to me swiftly, O God—why do You wait for that?
stc_090: How deep and dreadful by nature is saṃsāra’s ocean; who but supreme Maheśvara is the way across it?
stc_091: I bow to You, end of all completed deeds, destroyer of Madana, Gaṅgā-crowned, who acts rightly for the purpose.
stc_092: For those praying for a state beyond lordship, knowledge, detachment, and duty, O Lord, what highest goal except You?
stc_093: O Śambhu, who does not long for You, though able to bend a straw? Graced by Your will, who would not bear Brāhmī’s burden?
stc_094: Crowned by the jewel of reverence to Hara, unless rich in wisdom, whom would they honor as supreme, whom not honor?
stc_095: O Matted-haired Lord, enthroned amid the ocean of worldly knowledge, You are the still nectar-bestower that frees all delusion.
stc_096: Whatever wonder, whether beheld by strange sight or formed in mind, O Lord, You give as the fully fulfilled fruit of ultimate truth.
stc_097: Who surpasses You in qualities, or who, apart from You, is superior without qualities? O Lord, we bow; mind cannot praise or blame You.
stc_098: Even in Your praise, the nectar-flood yields such fruit of Your grace; who else could drink it, O Lord of worlds - what is there to give?
stc_099: From You, guide and treasury of fulfillment for every worthy aim, O Lord, I pray always to attain only devotion to You.
stc_100: O Lord of the three worlds, salutations to Your power that, for beings delighting in existence, takes on and removes world-lordship.
stc_101: O Master, in doubt over the cause of complete removal of afflictions, having known You are He - who has not gone to You for refuge?
stc_102: Having enjoyed pleasures and abandoned worldly delusion, I shall gain the supreme state; O Shambhu, may this hope be the devotee's highest adornment.
stc_103: O Lord, whatever I do or say, even in dreams, good or bad, with the proud assurance of belonging to You, I am content everywhere.
stc_104: O Lord, Light of lights, for one hastening to Your abode, I deem the mind's touch of darkness a barren woman's child - unreal.
stc_105: He who sets his foot on liberation's path and resolves firmly, 'I shall serve Shiva,' is safe too, I think.
stc_106: Here, in the three worlds' processes of maintenance, arising, and dissolution, You alone, O Lord, are the power of becoming; You behold the sovereign Tantra.
stc_107: Who here in the three worlds is a savior unburned by the three fires? Homage to You, the heart of the nectar of liberation.
stc_108: Even artificial devotion to You yields genuine fruit; if it is wholly sincere, what result? Please tell me.
stc_109: By that gaze You are seen, by that path You are reached; its fruit is unborn, sprung from the wish-fulfilling tree of Your speech.
stc_110: More blessed than blessing is this supreme abiding in You; O Lord, remover of obstacles to it, You are my refuge.
stc_111: Ah, most sweet is the nectar of all service and praise; at each instant, how could it not grow ever new?
stc_112: Who, again and again at rest, yet with hundreds of imaginings, projects the triple world? The one unborn, beyond conception, prevails.
stc_113: O God, when shall I stand before You through knowledge's lamp, burning the filthy oil-wick of samsaric tendencies?
stc_114: O Shambhu, when You set even one moment's step in a fault-free mind, what will You not accomplish?
stc_115: O Lord, may the thought 'I am blessed, my task accomplished, I am great' stand firm for one whose support is You.
stc_116: Though You Yourself are the doer of all good and ill, O Lord, devotion to You alone gives birth to auspiciousness.
stc_117: O Lord, when the mind is glad, why do You enter? People waver, thinking it will become glad by Your entering.
stc_118: Here again the sole certainty is Your sustaining presence; O Lord, the mind's gladness is fulfillment, the supreme state.
stc_119: O Lord, whatever my speech, mind, deed, and body, may they by Your grace become adorned only with devotion to You.
stc_120: O Shambhu, Bhatta Narayana composed this jewel of praise, abundantly granting desire-fruit and sheltering devotion's fortune.
rhs_01: At the Brahmā hour of dawn, surrender to the Goddess; then meditation, vows, and twilight rites; through the watches chant and worship; spend the rest as Śiva’s attendant.
rhs_02: May the Goddess, form of consciousness, Sarasvatī—whose face, hands, feet, limbs, and heart are made of syllables from A, Ka, Ṭa, Pa, and Ya—be victorious.
rhs_03: Wish-jewels, wish-cows, and desire-trees yield what men desire; may the Mother’s noble heart nourish in me unasked, unforeseen, worthy ends.
rhs_04: Without Her, the Lord of consciousness neither acts, nor knows, nor desires; salutations to Her, supreme Mother of worlds, to Śiva and Śiva’s beloved.
rhs_05: O ever-rising Goddess, all-auspicious, granter of Śiva, dwelling in Śiva’s heart, O lotus-opening moon: worship, O bird-mind, and guide my journey into the supreme sky.
rhs_06: Be pleased, O all-auspicious, O Auspicious One, beloved of Śiva, O Uma, Ramā, Sarasvatī: You alone are the supreme Goddess.
rhs_07: O Ame, Ambikā, beyond sound and form, nameless, Umā, Rodi, Vāmā, Mahālakṣmī, Māyā; O supreme Goddess, delighting in the five acts, Śiva, Bhairavī, Śrīmatī, I take refuge in You.
rhs_08: O Māyā, Vidyā, Mātṛkā, honored Lady, You throb in every body as consciousness’ subtlest art; how can we meditate on You, self-pulsing, inner speech resounding?
rhs_09: O Māyā, in this ever-afflicted body of skin, blood, flesh, fat, marrow, and bone, You drown ignorant beings in great hopes.
rhs_10: Seeing gods installed on iron tablets, some cry ‘Alas!’ and slay, thinking themselves fulfilled; whom does Māyā not fill with delusion among body-destroyers and body-sharers?
rhs_11: O Supreme Goddess, guard me from māyā's play, from the body born of hollow intellect, from ego's traces, from strain, from the form of self-awareness, and from falling and not falling.
rhs_12: He gazes, astonished, on the Dread Goddess, most dread and not dread, called supreme-and-limited, lower and highest, manifold in form, the glory of the two Śivas.
rhs_13: Amid the rays circling the supreme, the limited, and both, I disdain no division or non-division.
rhs_14: O Mother, fearless, boon-giving Supreme Goddess, protect the virtuous who remember both Your pulsing unsurpassed form and Your world-made form.
rhs_15: O Parameśvarī, Pārvatī, play of the five acts, made of supreme consciousness, be pleased; lift this fallen creature from the animal noose and comfort this child with Your cool hands and eyes.
rhs_16: Having bowed to the earlier perfected gurus, gods, Goddess, and yogins, I, Abhinavagupta, have spoken these fifteen verses.
dvd_01: When real, unreal, indescribable slumber, and quarrel dissolve, I am not troubled by 'What? How? Who am I?' Whatever shines unbroken through apparent being and nonbeing is void Śiva-abode, supreme reality; apart from Brahman, what meaning is there?
dvd_02: That which seeks reality by excluding the non-real is indeed the non-real; whether it is non-real or real, surely this is reality.
dvd_03: Whatever appears as other than the Light, in the Light it does not shine; what then is rejected but blame of breaking and unbreaking? A dream losing dreamness becomes play, not frightening with sword, water, fire, or bonds.
dvd_04: Whatever one meditates on, after devising meditation and ritual, tell me, what difference from inert matter? Is not even pulsing inertness the abode of indestructible awareness, limitless, eternal, ungraspable, true in form?
dvd_05: You reveal all mental states; whether their garland unfolds or not, your unbroken greatness remains, motiveless, beyond words, ever content through error, ever awake, O Lord.
dvd_06: Striking an evil target outwardly, or inwardly mimicking Bhairava, is sheer deception; faultless awareness' sky has no inside or outside, O spaceless radiance.
dvd_07: In the joyful spread of latent traces, whatever shines is That; in beginning, middle, and end, whether it appears or not, all dissolves in you.
dvd_08: If delusion, a dense mass of sorrowful reasoning, strung with endless errors, like a mirage-city, does not shine in consciousness' sky, where else could manifold being find final rest?
dvd_09: In dream, death is unreal; in the sushumna-light's path, beyond all description, consciousness' sky is blameless. In waking, like a pot's appearance, superimpositions cease, what negation remains?
dvd_10: Whatever lights shine in me, the supreme sky, undivided in my glory, O Lord, I am that: motiveless, eternal, unobstructed, infinite, truthful, free, demon-destroying, compassionate, boundless awareness-light.

mhu_01: Salutations to you, form beyond the world, embodiment of all, ever divine light, your own Self, infinite power.
mhu_02: You are You, I am I; You alone are, and I am not I. Where neither I nor you are, I bow again and again to That.
mhu_03: Within the body I ever sought You and the Self; neither You nor the Self was seen, yet whatever was seen was You alone.
mhu_04: As Your devotee who knows Your form, I again behold You as the Self; I bow again and again to You and to myself.
mhu_05: This clumsiness in movement, rooted in 'what must be done,' belongs to one whose self is Your maya: by whom, in whom, whence dissolution?
mhu_06: In 'I am You, You are I' there is no difference anywhere between the two; yet the wish to attain samadhi itself is where difference dwells.
mhu_07: Endless words like 'You are I, that is this' never find room in You; if speech cannot, whence the world?
mhu_08: Enough of speaking of difference, having savored the essence of devotion to You; even saying 'All this is one, peaceful' makes one ashamed.
mhu_09: When Your nature expands, You, I, and the whole world appear; when that expansion is veiled, there is neither You nor I nor world.
mhu_10: Sustaining waking, dream, deep sleep, and Your own faculties, by free will You shine like an actor, yet in truth You are partless.
mhu_11: Its awakening comes from Your awakening, its dissolution from Your sleep; therefore all this universe, consisting of being and nonbeing, is Your own self.
mhu_12: The tongue tires of Your name, the mind tires of remembering You; for the formless, where meditation? for the qualityless, what name?
mhu_13: Where invoke the All-full? What seat for the Support of all? What foot-water and offerings for the spotless? What sipping water for the pure?
mhu_14: Where bath for the stainless? What garment for the universe's belly? Where fragrance for the unblemished? What ornaments for the lovely One?
mhu_15: What sacred thread for the unsupported? What flower for the scentless? Where incense for the noseless? What lamp for the eyeless?
mhu_16: What food for the ever-satisfied? What betel for the Lord? Where circumambulation for the infinite, non-dual One? Where prostration?
mhu_17: Where lamp-offering for the self-luminous Lord? What hymns are made for the One beyond Vedic speech?
mhu_18: How dismiss the One full within and without? How offer fire to the undivided everywhere?
mhu_19: What gift for the complete One? What satisfaction for the ever-satisfied? Where dismissal for the all-pervading? What pardon for the unseen?
mhu_20: This is supreme worship in all states, always: with oneness of mind, fix the mind on God, the Lord of all.
psl_01: O Lord, beyond the truth I have done and my mind's devoted offering at Isha's lotus feet, there is no duty; that is all my wealth. O truthful One, refuge of the helpless, ocean of compassion, be pleased swiftly.
psl_02: O Mahesha, may beautiful, faultless speech ever resound at your door: Victory, victory, Mahesha! May this auspicious word be ever auspicious for me; O refuge-giver, make me, without another lord, permanently sheltered.
psl_03: No reply, no sight of my distress; though I plead many ways, you neither hear nor approach my mind. Fallen in samsara's abyss, you do not uphold me; Scripture says you are without speech, sight, hearing, hands.
psl_04: Through the guru's word, which dispels contrived reasoning, and fitting scripture that consoles, may my mind touch the feet of the great Sun-Lord, risen in the heart-sky when doubt-clouds dissolve, conqueror of darkness.
psl_05: With you, O wind, ages pass like moments; through worshipping the supreme guru, you have done much for me. Yet seeing divine realms, I often forget you with this body, so I should not stay.
kra_01: Now is the time for taking food at the end of the having come to the end of observing the vow of crossing over the array of troubles. kra_02: The devotee contemplates on himself and then on the actions of the deity. Thus, he gives expression only to his sense of difference from the deity. kra_03: Until its elimination the Self does not become the sharer in the sense of the Reality. The Self remains intact until the devotee undergoes the due course of contemplation. kra_05: Having dispelled this status of mine termed as bondage and having turned into the joy of life by means of application of the endless fire of prayer eliminative of all sense of difference between me and the Lord and having expanded my awareness of you with all its peculiarity, I am tasting the essence of being, O bestower of boons, and now am maddened out of joy.
kra_06: If the peculiar tale of accomplishments of the Lord were to ascend the heart which is promotive of the awareness of His mighty force of glory involved in the creation, how can one pray to Him and if even then one ventures to do it all of a sudden on having attained oneness with Siva, the way to it is simply obeisance to Him.
kra_07: ...... Burning, shining and heating are the qualities inherent in fire except for which the form of fire cannot be conceived. Likewise, I pray to rays of consciousness to make manifest its illumination except for which there does not remain anything glorious in the Lord.
kra_08: ---:- The supernal consciousness is replete with invaluable qualities of doing miraculous acts like breaking all laws and yet creating the state of delight, absolute perfection in the midst of the opposite boundlessness, self-luminosity and yet the sense of unity in the midst of the entire diversity of objects.
kra_09: O Lord, manifesting itself in such contradictory forms in various ways, this world is a part of yourself without any difference from you. Praying to you, as such, kindly make my heart and organs of sense remain engaged continuously with full force at their disposal.
kra_10: It is the sea of your consciousness in its various displays of vibrations and withdrawal which is manifesting itself automatically in various kinds of homogeneity. It is these manifestations of yourself which are taking the form of creation, sustenance and dissolution in the form of daily rising and setting of the sun and moon and burning and getting extinguished in the form of fire.
kra_11: O Bhairava, may you be merciful on me in keeping your force continuously remain the same without any difference from you in all its variations of peculiarity and symmetry in course of its operation in the form of the universe. In this state of play of variations, may you make me concentratingly abide in my heart which is the field of operation of your forces as unrelated with anything.
kra_12: It is you yourself who differentiates your Force from you which really does never go apart from you in course of observation of the magnificent ceremony of experience of delight under the motivation of your own wish.
kra_13: Your manifestation in the form of the objective world, O Lord, is replete with joy. There is nothing like seriality in you. As such, there is no place for the sense of time in you. You lie beyond the reach of the power of mind and speech and thus beyond the reach of organs of sense. Therefore, your form as jars, etc. remain continuously present all together.
kra_14: Creating the sense of seriality on this background resulting in the sense of difference you, O Lord, are manifesting your own Forces continuously well within yourself in the form of action, knowledge and will corresponding to sustenance, dissolution and magnified form of creation. My heart, O Lord, is eager to remain concentrated to this triplicity of Forces of yours.
kra_15: May this higher creation accomplished by fire manifesting itself in the form of supernal delight owing to touch of the moon with it, as the manifestation of yours known as creation with the combination of the attributes of the fire and the moon (amounting to Soma) expand its splendour before me.
kra_16: The integrality of existence has assumed the form of the creation of the multiplicity which outwardly is extremely tasteless. kra_17: In order to get redeemed of the tendency of externality of the curvature of consciousness and dwell durably in pure consciousness, you, O Lord when you expand the sense of non-difference with the entire being having stopped the vibration in its entirety while the Goddess of manifestation seeks to stop the sense of durability, O Lord, may you contemplate on destroying the sense of worldliness lurking in me for ever.
kra_18: O Lord, bring consolidation to posterity and negativity towards the world by means of dissolution of the world forcefully. Having recreated the world and thus having dispelled the doubt of being and non-being, may the great Goddess eliminate the fear of worldliness from me.
kra_19: Following vanishment of the cloud of doubt and full flourishing of the glory, elimination of the worldliness and rejection of the rules of the scriptural writings, the Lord may eliminate from my heart the elements of worldliness of difference from you.
kra_20: ---:--- In this way, following removal of the expansion of difference altogether by the Goddess from my heart, the status of the Mother with alternative as Her main spirit may prevail over me. Therefore, having contemplated over worldliness in Her heart, She with all the sense of durability in Her may be pleased gladly with me as the agent of elimination of the incidence of death.
kra_21: Thus, these three goddesses by way of manifesting their glory have assumed the form of the six centres (cakras) in the central nerve known as SU$umnii by piercing which one after the other the yogin attains peculiar states of consciousness on the earth. kra_22: I have stopped the effect of the earth on me on account of which gets eliminated the fear of worldliness. Consequently, I have reached the state of oneness with the Supreme Lord and enjoy the state of delight experienced by me. kra_23: May consciousness which dissolves within itself the functions of organs of action, sense and intellect, etc. which have attained their respectable statuses within their respective limitations. kra_24: May the Goddess of consciousness be pleased with me and adorn the seat of my heart who having withdrawn to Herself simultaneously all the awareness of the group of sense organs manifests Her entire wealth of rays so that She may lead one to the state of divine delight out of Her generosity.
kra_25: On elimination of all the measurements of validity owing to attainment of the glorious state of Siva-hood, the body, life-force, etc. as components of the limited sense of the knower get dissolved along with the superimposition of the sense of time, then that Goddess of consciousness manifests Herself in Her fullness. May She be one with Siva for me.
kra_26: May the magnanimous Kali, as luminous consciousness rid of seriality having vanished outside moving from Her state of vacuity expand Herself fully as the coverage shorn of process in Her real essence remove the obstacle of time from my life.
kra_27: Therefore, the Goddess enjoying Her status in the highest possible state of perfection having removed seriality from Herself as soon as possible may be stable in me. Having eliminated the distinction of standard of validity, the knower, and the act of knowing and thus taking the entire world inside Her lap take resort to my inner being in the form of its consciousness.
kra_28: I pay my obeisance to the Lord who lies there possessed of His infinite Force and acts as the instrument of churning of the world into one essence.

shivastotravali_18_1: Jagadīśa, O Lord of the universes, O Lord of one hundred and eighteen worlds, tavaiva bhakti-bhājo, those are Your real devotees who find You amidst the state of the universe, amidst the universal state. …
shivastotravali_18_2: At some places, from one point of view, it seems that You are the only person existing in this universe. From another point of view, it seems that the universe is only existing.
shivastotravali_18_3: Avalepavantaḥ lokāḥ, those people who have got avalepa, who have got impurity in their minds, those persons who have got impurity in their minds, they don’t understand, they don’t experience subhagamapi; subhagamapi rūpaṁ no jānanti, they don’t experience that sweet and wonderful nature of God because prayatna subhagā hi nikhilā bhāvāḥ, this whole collection of universal objects becomes refined and sweet only by meditation, by the effort of meditation.
shivastotravali_18_4: There is such a devotee in this universe who bhavanmaya svātmanivāsalabdha sampadbharābhyarcita yuṣmat aṅghriḥ, who is residing in the nature of the Self, which is one with Your nature. …
shivastotravali_18_5: Eṣa lokaḥ, this worldly group of people, worldly ignorant group of people, although those are bhavat deha svasthopi, they are residing, actually they are residing, in Your nature–everybody is residing in the nature of Lord Śiva, in reality; in reality, everyone is there–although this worldly ignorant group resides in Your nature and has actually achieved a peaceful state by being in Your nature, but antaḥ paraṁ dahyate, but internally [they are] tortured and sentenced to crises and sadness, i.e., these worldly people. And this is Your desire; this is Your desire, by Your will. This does not take place according to their karmas. This takes place according to Your sweet will.
shivastotravali_18_6: My Lord, this is one desire in me: svarasodita yuṣmat aṅghri padma dvaya pūjā amṛta pāna saktaḥ cittaḥ, my mind should be directed towards tasting the nectar of worshiping Your lotus feet. …
shivastotravali_18_7: O my Master, prabho, O my Master, there is another desire in me. That is, sakala vyavahāragocare sphuṭamantaḥ sphurati tvayi prabho, You must appear to me, I wish You appear to me, in each and every action of universality. …
shivastotravali_18_8: This is another desire knocking in the background of my heart. That is, satatameva tavaiva pure’thavā pyarahito vicareyam ahaṁ tvayā, I should always roam in Your kingdom. I want to roam and walk and rest and do all things in Your kingdom. …
shivastotravali_18_9: Now, You will say that, “It is not possible to be attached to Me always. I have never been like that with any other devotee”. …
shivastotravali_18_10: Nātha, O my Master, there is one desire in me. I want to remain in that great forest, in the grand forest, of Thee. The grand forest, he says, that dense forest is Your body. …
shivastotravali_18_11: It is a fact that in each and every object (prativastū, in each and every object), to each and every being (samastajīvataḥ), You appear in the form of jñāna (knowledge).
shivastotravali_18_12: I have acquired something, which I want to offer to You. This is my offering for You. That is, caru (sweet cake), the sweet cake which I have acquired in my whole life, that is the ego in me. …
shivastotravali_18_13: There is another problem in me. I would like to reside in the ocean of supreme nectar, that supreme nectar (nivasan parama [amṛta], that supreme nectar). Parama amṛta abdhimadhye, I would like to reside in the center of the ocean of Thy nectar.
shivastotravali_18_14: Thy reality, let Thy reality reside where It is. Bhavadīyamihāstu vastu tattvam, let Thy reality reside where It is because vivarītuṁ ka ivātra pātramarthe, who can define That? Who can define Your reality? That is so great. …
shivastotravali_18_16: These states of life, jāgara (jāgara means “wakefulness”), itaradaśā (itaradaśā means “the dreaming state”), and the dreamless state (suṣupti), yāpi kācana manāg avasthiteḥ, or other than these three states, which are existing in the cycle of daily life, all of those states become, to those who are bhakti bhājana janasya (bhakti bhājana janasya [means “those] who are just befitting, who are just capable of, becoming the containing pot of Thy devotion”; in brief words, “those who are Your devotees”), for those devotees, all of these states–wakefulness, the dreaming state, and the dreamless state, and all of the other states of daily life also–tvatsanātha manasaḥ mahotsavaḥ . . .
shivastotravali_18_17: O my Master, this is a wonder to me. …

shivastotravali_18_19: There is one desire in me. That desire is, I would like to clean the impurity of my mind, the impurity of my vikalpa (thoughts)–that is mind.
shivastotravali_18_20: Nātha, O Lord, could You do one thing for me? That is, get entry in my body. You enter in my body, then, after Your entrance, after You enter in my body, I will enter in You. …

shivastotravali_19_1: Śiva is really [like] the pārijāta tree.
shivastotravali_19_2: O Lord, this is a fact that because You are the treasure of everything, You are the treasure of all the universal things–all universal objects are found, are treasured, in You–and from That treasure, everything is achieved (tvat svātmanastvad akhilaṁ kila labhyam, everything is achieved). shivastotravali_19_4: Nātha, O my Master, tvat dṛgātmanā, there is a path, there is one path, which is the path of understanding You, Your existence. …

shivastotravali_19_6: Nātha, O my Master, when that day will come when I will be perceiving or seeing Your pure face (mukhabiṁbam, I would perceive Your pure face)? …
shivastotravali_19_7: O my Lord, I have created some trouble in my mind and that is due to tvat avibheda vimokṣa akhyāti; tvat avibheda, being deprived of Your oneness. …
shivastotravali_19_8: Nātha, O Master, my mind has not yet become tvadīya anuttara rasa āsaṅga santyakta cāpalam, my mind has not removed the cañcalatā.
shivastotravali_19_9: All dvandvas, all opposite things in this universe . . .
shivastotravali_19_10: O my Master, let Your rays shine and come near to me always, up to that moment when kāyamanastāpa tamobhiḥ, the darkness and sadness of my mind and body would be gone.
shivastotravali_19_11: O Lord, I am looted by these thieves, the thieves of the senses of the organs. These senses of the organs are thieves because they are thieves and they have looted all of my wealth.
shivastotravali_19_12: These limited desires, which are existing in individuals–e.g., I want a child, I want a wife, I want a car, I want a good job, all of these things, all of these are limited things, very limited things, and they are not stable, they always come and go–and these desires, they have a similarity with those haṁsas (swans). Niḥśeṣāsāravāsanā, these are asāra vāsanā (vāsanā means these “desires” and asāra [means] “with no substance in them, with no reality in them”), and they are [existing] in that mind, which is a lake without water. shivastotravali_19_14: Vibho, O Lord Śiva, siddhilavalābhalubdhaṁ māmavalepena mā vibho saṁsthāḥ, let me not become attached to these limited powers, yogic powers. …

shivastotravali_20_1: Nāthaṁ vande, I bow to my Master who is the Master of all the three worlds (tribhuvana nātham), bhūtisitam, whose body is white because of rubbing that vibhūti (bhasma).
shivastotravali_20_2: Nija tanu vinissarat aṁśuka pariveṣa dhavala paridhānam. …

shivastotravali_20_5: Nātha, O Master, viśvavandye tvaddhāmni, in Your kingdom, which is adored by each and every being–Your kingdom is adored and appreciated by each and every individual; Your kingdom is not denied–and in this viśvavandye (viśvavandye means “adored by viśva, adored by the whole universe”), and in Your kingdom, iyati krīḍane sati, this whole creation of this universe (e.g., beautiful flowers, beautiful ladies, beautiful people, beautiful birds, beautiful songs, beautiful music, etc.), this is only Your one particle of Your play! shivastotravali_20_6: Now, there is one more thing to be explained by [Utpaladeva].
shivastotravali_20_7: Now, he explains here that a devotee of Lord Śiva is just like a beautiful tree–a beautiful, glorious tree–and that glorious tree, the roots of that glorious tree (that is, Your devotee), the roots of that glorious tree are soaked with Thy meditation, with the nectar of Thy meditation, because those devotees always meditate on Your form, on Your being. So, this nectar is always there at the root of that tree.
shivastotravali_20_8: O Lord Śiva, when a devotee of Thee has created this [itching] sensation of bhakti (devotion), and that itching won’t be removed until You are there, You are present. Your main presence will remove that itching sensation.
shivastotravali_20_9: I bow to my master who is always enjoying the act of creation (the act of creating this whole universe), who is always absorbed in protecting it, and who is always bent upon destroying it.

shivastotravali_20_11: Those who are glorified with the wealth of Thy devotion (bhakti lakṣmī samṛddhānām, those who are glorified with the wealth of Your devotion), kim anyat upayācitam, what do they need? What else [do] they need? …
shivastotravali_20_12: On that path, on that pathway, where duḥkhāni api sukhāyante, pains, various pains, are transformed into various enjoyments, viṣamapi, and this poison becomes nectar on which path various pains are transformed into the shape of enjoyments, and on which path this poison takes the formation of nectar, and on which path, this universe, [which] is the only cause of getting you entangled in the wheel of repeated deaths and births, liberates you . . .*

shivastotravali_20_16: Īśa, O Lord Śiva, that supreme I-consciousness, which is sarvāvabhāsa, which [illuminates] this whole universe, which is the cause of [illuminating] this whole universe (it is sarva avabhāsa avabhāva, [which is] aham, I-consciousness, I-God consciousness), vimarśa valito, although this is filled with vimarśa338, . . .
